setup: High plank, hands under your shoulders
Straight line from head to heels
execution: Drive one knee toward your chest
Switch legs in a quick, steady rhythm
Keep your hips level with your shoulders
faults: Don't pike your hips up high
Don't let your shoulders drift behind your hands

notes: Pick a pace you can keep with a steady plank; speed up only while the hips stay level.
If your wrists are uncomfortable, put your hands on a step or bench, or use push-up handles.
Fast intervals raise breathing and heart rate quickly. Rest until your breathing settles.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move
Chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure in a high plank facing right. Hands stay planted; only the legs alternate.

keyPositions.label: Near knee in
keyPositions.describe: High plank, arms straight with hands under the shoulders. Near knee drawn toward the chest, foot off the floor. Far leg straight behind on the ball of the foot. Hips level with the shoulders.

keyPositions.label: Far knee in
keyPositions.describe: Mirror: far knee drawn toward the chest, near leg straight behind. Hips still level; shoulders still over the hands.

ikHints: Hands fixed on the floor in every frame
Hip height constant within about ±3% of body height
emphasise: Hips level with the shoulders the whole time
Knees drive under the chest in turn
doNotShow: Feet slapping far forward past the hands

sources.note: Seen through a search-result summary; the library page and its RSS feed disagree on difficulty.

uncertain.note: The expansion research lists hip flexors as a primary muscle; the catalogue has no hip_flexors word (Q1), so they are left out. front_delts reflects the shoulders holding the plank, reasoned from the position rather than measured.
Timed by default, as in class and circuit use. Some people count reps; logging those would need a reps entry or a change of measurement.
Stride tempo, slowed for readability; real intervals often run faster. Angles are approximate drawing targets.
